questions.question: How can you best tell if your trailer is starting to skid?

options.text: Look in your mirrors to see if the trailer has moved out of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look in your mirrors to see if the trailer has moved out of the lane.
questions.explanation: Using your mirrors is the easiest way to notice a skid. Checking your mirrors lets you spot skidding as early as possible.

questions.question: What does the trailer air supply control look like?
questions.correctAnswerText: An eight-sided red knob.
questions.explanation: The trailer air supply control is an eight-sided red knob on newer vehicles. It controls the tractor protection valve.

questions.question: What should you do after finishing a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Leave the rear shut-off valves open.
Leave the emergency line valve open.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the emergency line valve.
questions.explanation: Before driving, open the rear emergency line and service line shut-off valves to check for air leaks. Close both valves before you start driving.

questions.question: When driving slower than 40 mph, keep at least ____ of space for every 10 feet of your vehicle length.
questions.correctAnswerText: One second
questions.explanation: Below 40 mph, allow one second of space for every 10 feet of vehicle length. At faster speeds, use the same formula and add one more second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop.

questions.question: Which trailer is most likely to flip over when a driver turns too quickly?
questions.correctAnswerText: Last
questions.explanation: When turning, steer gently and smoothly. Quick turns while pulling trailers are dangerous and can cause the last trailer to roll over.

questions.question: What happens if you use the trailer hand brake during a jackknife?
questions.correctAnswerText: It continues the skid.
questions.explanation: During a jackknife, release the brakes to help your tires grip the road again. Using the trailer hand brake during a skid will only make it worse.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?

options.text: When a truck driver is driving too fast.
When the vehicle in front is moving too slowly.
When a truck driver is driving too slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a truck driver is driving too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when driving too fast. To prevent rollovers, load cargo low to the ground and take turns and curves slowly.

questions.question: What does the tractor protection valve do?

options.text: Stops the tractor from being stolen.
Stops the tractor from going too fast.
Keeps air in the braking system if the trailer breaks away or leaks.
Makes sure the engine has enough oil.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps air in the braking system if the trailer breaks away or leaks.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor braking system if the trailer breaks away or develops a bad leak.

questions.question: What does having anti-lock brakes on only one axle do?

options.text: Does not make a difference in braking.
Gives you more control when braking.
Likely causes the air brakes to break.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you more control when braking.
questions.explanation: Having anti-lock brakes on just one axle still gives you more control during braking than having no anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: What happens when you push in the trailer air supply control?
questions.correctAnswerText: Air flows to the trailer.
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull it out to stop the air supply and turn on the emergency brakes.

questions.question: When braking with ABS, you should:

options.text: Press the brake pedal harder than normal.
Press the brake pedal as you normally would.
Press the brake pedal lighter than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brake pedal as you normally would.
questions.explanation: With ABS, brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: ____ cause more than half of all truck driver deaths in accidents.
questions.correctAnswerText: Truck rollovers
questions.explanation: Truck rollovers cause more than half of all truck driver deaths in accidents. To prevent a rollover, keep cargo low and centered. Turn corners slowly and carefully.

questions.question: Combination vehicles:

options.text: Usually have taller trailers than single commercial vehicles.
Are usually lighter than single commercial vehicles.
Require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles require more skill to drive. They are longer, heavier, and more likely to rollover.

questions.question: Set the trailer air supply control to "emergency" position to test:
questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer emergency brakes.
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before each trip. Make sure the trailer rolls freely first. Then pull out the trailer air supply control or set it to "emergency." Pull forward slightly with the tractor. The trailer should not move.

questions.question: When connecting a converter dolly to a second trailer, the trailer height should be ____ the center of the fifth wheel.
questions.correctAnswerText: Slightly lower than
questions.explanation: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, the trailer height should be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve should:

options.text: Be used only to test the trailer brakes.
Be used together with the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used only to test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve controls the trailer brakes but should only be used when testing them. Using it while driving can cause a skid. Do not use it while parking because it may release air pressure and cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: When lightly loaded, combination vehicles:

options.text: Should be loaded with most of the weight in the rear of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have reduced braking capabilities.
questions.explanation: Lightly loaded combination vehicles have poor traction. The wheels can lock up easily when stopping.

questions.question: After connecting the air lines to the trailer while coupling, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Supply air to the trailer.
questions.explanation: Follow the correct steps to couple and uncouple trailers safely. After connecting the air lines to the trailer, supply air to the trailer.

questions.question: To prevent a trailer from rolling over, you should:

options.text: Speed up when nearing a corner.
Take on-ramps faster than the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly around corners.
questions.explanation: To reduce rollover risk, keep cargo low and centered. Drive slowly around turns.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve should be used:

options.text: Regularly to activate the trailer brakes in all driving conditions.
Only to test the trailer brakes.
Only in bad weather when the trailer may skid.
Only if the trailer is carrying a load.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: Use the trailer hand valve only to test the trailer brakes. Do not use it while driving because it may cause the trailer to skid.

questions.question: How should you use the brakes in a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: The same way you would brake in a vehicle without ABS.
While the vehicle is in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way you would brake in a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: Brake the same way in a vehicle with ABS as you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: What does a tractor protection valve do?

options.text: It keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak.
It prevents a truck from being stolen.
It prevents the driver from driving too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: It keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak.
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a bad leak. The valve closes automatically when the pressure becomes unsafe.

questions.question: When should you use a trolley valve?

options.text: Only to test the trailer brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trolley valve controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Do not use it while driving because it can cause a skid. Do not use it while parking because it may release the air pressure and cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: Are trailers built before 1975 required to have spring brakes?

options.text: Yes, they are required to have spring brakes.
No, they are not required to have spring brakes.
They are not allowed on public roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, they are not required to have spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built before 1975 are not required to have spring brakes. When parking a trailer without spring brakes, use wheel chocks to keep it from rolling.

questions.question: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, what should the trailer height be?

options.text: Slightly higher than the center of the fifth wheel.
Level with the center of the fifth wheel.
Slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.
Next to the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: The trailer height should be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel when connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer.
